package.title: 4x faster analysis loop, stable custom palettes, safe palette replacement
package.goal: The analysis loop runs about 4x faster with bit-identical output. A palette the user built keeps every colour, its order and its codes through a compute. 'Palette aus Materialien' and colour removal can no longer silently scramble the stones.
steps: FIRST, before any change: write tests/w1-mosaic-core.test.ts. It computes the four samples (tests/helpers prepareFor, Home presets, seed 7) and hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code. Store the hashes in tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json.

Hot loop: replace mosaic.ts:217-219 `groupOf(() => 0, 1)[0]` with a scalar summation loop over SL/SA/SB, using the same formula and order. In the LINE search (mosaic.ts:327-330) set gA.n = cnt and gB.n = NS - cnt instead of reading counts from the Float64Array. Optional: monomorphic groupOf with an Int8Array of labels. Accept it only if the hashes stay identical.

Custom mode: add `code?: number` to FixedColor. When paletteMode === 'custom', skip the used-filter, the L* sort and the remap. Keep the input order. Set code = fixed[i].code when all codes are unique positive integers, otherwise i+1. Keep hex, name and materialId. Leave the other modes unchanged. Wave 2 passes p.code from useProject.

paletteOps.ts: add mergePaletteFromMaterials(palette, data|null, materials, formula) returning {palette, movedStones, maxDeltaE}. It appends missing materials with addPaletteColor and removes palette entries with no material counterpart through removePaletteColor in DESCENDING index order. Existing indices therefore stay valid and only removed colours are remapped.

StepColors 'Palette aus Materialien': when api.computed exists, use the merge, ask for confirmation first (stone count to be moved, max ΔE), then setPalette and touchMosaic. Otherwise keep the current replace.

StepColors remove(): show a confirm dialog with the stone count of the colour and the replacement colour code. Offer a choice of replacement through removePaletteColor's replacement argument. Mark palette rows with 0 stones as 'nicht verwendet'.
acceptance: Golden hashes are identical after the hot-loop change, i.e. bit-identical output.
A scratch tsx bench at about 1.2M cells shows analyze time at most 40 % of the old time. Note the result in the PR; it is not a CI test.

Custom palette of 8 colours with codes [1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9] and one colour no stone can use (pure yellow on the portrait): the result has 8 entries in input order with the same codes, yellow has 0 pieces, and per-colour counts match the old implementation by hex. A second compute with the returned palette gives the identical palette.

Merge test: compute custom mode from 12 materials, then merge with a reduced material list. The moved-stone count equals the stones of the removed colours, the total is unchanged, and every index is < palette.length.
Auto-mode outputs equal the golden fixture.
package.risk: Effort M. Record the golden hashes before touching the code. Custom palettes stay correct across recompute only once wave 2 passes p.code through; until then codes become i+1, which is still stable for palettes without gaps.

findings.title: Compute at 2M–5M positions spends almost all its time in shape analysis that finds almost no cuts, on one core
findings.problem: The analysis loop always takes 6x6 bilinear samples per cell when shapes are enabled (mosaic.ts:127). For any cell above the SSE threshold it tries two diagonals, three line angles and subdivision. The line search allocates per cell and angle (Array.from(order).sort and new Float64Array, mosaic.ts:308 to 310) and counts linearly for each offset (mosaic.ts:325). At large grids the working image has only about 0.1 to 3 source pixels per cell (workingSize is capped at 6 MP or at the photo size), so sub-cell edges cannot be resolved, yet the full search still runs. Everything runs in one worker even though the 64x64 tiles are independent.
findings.evidence: Browser 5M (1250x1000 cm, 4 mm, portrait sample; quick-compute.cjs): compute 26.4 s, of which the analyze phase is 24.4 s (palette 0.19 s, assign 1.55 s). Diagnostics report 'Zellen mit Schnitt 23' out of 5,004,501 cells. Node 2M with a 12 MP photo, 3 px per cell (bench-core.ts): analyze 8.97 s with shapes on versus 4.79 s with shapes off, and 0 split cells in both runs. 5M: 7.67 s versus 3.71 s, 0 splits. CPU profile at 2M (prof-compute.ts): the analysis closures and loop take 72.5 % of samples. The machine has 4 cores (nproc=4), but only one is used. Paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: (a) Choose the sample grid from pixel density: S = clamp(round(2·sqrt(source px per cell)), 2, 6). When there are fewer than about 2 source pixels per cell, skip the shape search and state honestly in the diagnostics: 'Photo resolution too low for edge cuts at this grid (x px per stone)'. (b) Split the tile loop across navigator.hardwareConcurrency − 1 workers: share the Lab image as a SharedArrayBuffer, or transfer row bands with a one-cell halo. Each worker writes kind, c1Lab, c2Lab and the sub/line results for its band; then run k-means and assignment in one worker. That is about 3x on 4 cores. (c) In the line search, reuse preallocated order and prefix buffers, sort the indices once per angle with a typed-array sort, and advance cnt monotonically across offsets instead of restarting at 0.
corrected:
Fix the cause in the hot loop. Drop (a) and (c). Postpone (b).

1. src/core/mosaic.ts:327 and 329-330: build the line-search groups with integer counts. Use `gA = { n: cnt, sl: pre[cnt*5+1], ... }` and `gB = { n: NS - cnt, ... }` instead of `n: pre[cnt*5]` and `n: pre[tot] - gA.n`. The values are numerically identical, because the prefix count equals cnt. With this alone, analyze takes 3.25 s instead of 9.0 s at 2M and 8.7 s instead of 26.3 s at 5M, with byte-identical results.

2. src/core/mosaic.ts:217: compute the whole-cell statistics in a plain loop over SL/SA/SB, summing into local numbers. Today this goes through groupOf(() => 0, 1)[0], which per cell allocates an array and an object and calls a function that is shared with the search's closures. Better still, give groupOf precomputed Int8Array labels per partition (diagonal A/B, sub-grid) instead of per-cell closures. The labels depend only on S and the cell's aspect ratio, so they can be cached for uniform grids. Doing steps 1 and 2 together gives 5M analyze 7.4 s in Node and 6.8 s in Chromium.

3. Add a test that checks the output hash before and after the change (kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, palette), using a project with many split cells such as the portrait at 35k cells. Add a bench script that is not run in CI (for example tests/bench-compute.ts) and prints analyze time with shapes on and off at about 500k cells, so this 3x cliff can be caught if it comes back.

4. Keep S = 6 and keep running the shape search. It costs under 0.5 % of analyze time.
- If adaptive sampling is still wanted, allow only even values of S (2, 4 or 6) so that the k=2 sub-grid stays possible.
- Only add the low-resolution diagnostics note ('Photo resolution too low for edge cuts at this grid, x px per stone') as information. It is not a speed-up.
- Do not use the line-search buffer reuse from (c). It targets 1 to 91 ms.

5. Reconsider splitting across workers, item (b), only after steps 1 and 2. At that point Chromium computes 5M in about 9 s. Each worker would also need the fix from steps 1 and 2.

1. (S, do this first) In src/core/mosaic.ts:217-219, replace `const all = groupOf(() => 0, 1)[0]; const mean = meanOf(all); const fullSSE = sse(all);` with a loop that sums directly:
   `let tl=0,ta=0,tb=0,tq=0; for (let k=0;k<NS;k++){const l=SL[k],a=SA[k],b=SB[k]; tl+=l; ta+=a; tb+=b; tq+=l*l+a*a+b*b;} const mean: Lab=[tl/NS,ta/NS,tb/NS]; const fullSSE=tq-(tl*tl+ta*ta+tb*tb)/NS;`
   It uses the same formula and the same summation order as before, so the output is bit-identical. Measured: 5M cells go from 33 s to 8 s in Chromium, 2M analyze from 9.1 s to 2.25 s.

2. (S) Add a determinism test in tests/pipeline.test.ts, recorded with the current code before the change. For the four sample projects (default settings, seed 7), hash data.kind, c1, c2, the line and sub maps and the palette, and assert the stored golden hashes. This proves this optimisation, and any later one, changes no stone, cut or count.

3. (M, optional) Make groupOf monomorphic. Pass a reusable Int8Array of per-sample labels (filled per cell for diagA, diagB and the sub-grid) instead of a closure, and accumulate into a preallocated Float64Array(5*k*k) instead of creating objects with Array.from. Also reuse the line-search order and prefix buffers and keep `cnt` running across offsets (part c, measured about 3 %, identical hash). Accept only if the golden hashes stay the same.

4. Do NOT change S based on pixel density and do NOT skip the shape search for speed. The search is under 1 % of the time, and S values that are not multiples of subdivK silently disable subdivision (mosaic.ts:140/355). If an honest note about resolution is wanted, make it a separate diagnostic only: show the "Arbeitsauflösung: x px je Stein" (processed px / cells) in StepCompute. Below about 1 px per stone, warn whether the limit is the photo itself or the 6 MP working cap in imagePrep.ts:146. Leave the algorithm unchanged.

5. Defer splitting across several workers. SharedArrayBuffer is not available (no COOP/COEP headers, crossOriginIsolated is false, and the Capacitor WebView is the same). After step 1, the remaining big costs at 5M are stats (about 4-6 s) and assignment (about 1.8 s). If this is revisited, transfer row bands with a one-pixel halo and merge kind/c1Lab/c2Lab/sub/line in order, then check against the golden hashes.

6. After step 1, re-measure and update the README limitations line ("getestet bis 2 Mio.") with the real timings at 2M and 5M.

findings.title: Own palette ('Eigene Palette') loses unused colours and renumbers its codes on every Berechnen
findings.problem: In 'custom' mode (and 'materials' mode) computeMosaic drops every palette entry that no stone uses, sorts the rest by L* and renumbers them 1..n. useProject then saves res.palette as the project palette and uses rec.palette as the custom palette for the next run. So the user's own colours and numbers (requirement 7: '01=Weiss') are lost for good after one compute: a colour that is unused once can never come back, and a code can point to a different colour after a recompute. Separately, nextCode() = max(code)+1 gives a deleted colour's code to the next new colour, so sheets printed earlier (requirement 10: print sections separately) no longer match the legend.
findings.evidence: src/core/mosaic.ts:549-582 (used[] filter, keep.sort by L*, code: ni + 1); src/ui/project/useProject.ts:295 (custom: fixed = r.palette) and :333 (palette: res.palette). Core repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/r8_custom_palette.ts -> 'custom palette before compute: 01=Weiss, 02=Schwarz, 03=Rot, 04=Hellblau, 05=Gruen' / 'after compute #1: palette = 01=Hellblau, 02=Rot' (Rot changes from 03 to 02; three colours are deleted). Browser check (vite preview build) b1_custom_palette.cjs in the same folder: portrait sample, Eigene Palette, 3 colours added (35 rows) -> after Berechnen 31 rows and 0 of the added colours remain; screenshot b1_after.png shows 'Farblegende (31)'. Code reuse: t6_edits.out 'code of removed last colour was 10 -> new colour gets code 10' (src/core/edits.ts:142-144).
findings.proposal: Add `code?: number` to FixedColor (mosaic.ts:16) and pass p.code from useProject.ts:295. In computeMosaic, run the drop-unused + sort + renumber block (549-582) only for paletteMode 'auto'/'auto-snap'. For 'custom' and 'materials', keep every entry in its input order with its input code and only map indices; unused colours show 0 stones. Store a monotonically increasing `nextCode` counter in ProjectRecord and use it in addPaletteColor instead of max+1, so codes are never reused. Add a unit test: custom palette of 5 with 2 used -> 5 entries, codes unchanged, 0 pieces for the unused 3.
corrected:
Change custom mode only. Leave 'auto', 'auto-snap' and 'materials' as they are: in those modes the palette is rebuilt from k-means or the material database on every compute, so dropping unused colours is the right behaviour.
1) src/core/mosaic.ts:16: add `code?: number` to FixedColor. At lines 467-468, carry `code` into paletteMeta.
2) src/core/mosaic.ts:549-582: if params.paletteMode === 'custom', skip the used-filter, the L* sort and the remap. Keep the input order, and set each entry to `code: meta.code ?? i+1` with its input hex, name and materialId. The c1/c2/sub indices already point into the input array, so no remap is needed. Run the existing block only for the other modes.
3) src/ui/project/useProject.ts:295: pass `code: p.code` into `fixed`. Lines 333 and 339 can stay as they are, because res.palette now equals the input palette apart from Lab rounding.
4) Make unused colours visible but harmless. In StepColors, rows with 0 stones already show "–" or 0. In pdf.ts:320-326 (legend table), either filter `stats.perColor[i].pieces > 0` or list those rows with 0 under an "unbenutzt" note, so the printed legend stays short.
5) Optional, low priority: replace nextCode() = max+1 (edits.ts:142) with a `nextColorCode` counter stored on ProjectRecord (initialised to max(code)+1 when missing), so a deleted code is never given to a new colour.
6) Tests: in tests/, add a custom palette of 5 colours where the image uses only 2. Expect 5 entries in input order with codes 1..5 unchanged, 0 pieces for the other 3, and an identical palette after a second compute that feeds res.palette back in. Add a regression test that 'materials' mode still lists only the materials that are used.

1) src/core/mosaic.ts: add `code?: number` to the `FixedColor` interface (line 16). In the clean-up block (lines 549-582) set `const stable = params.paletteMode === 'custom'`. When stable is true:
   - `keep` = all input indices in input order, with no used-filter and no L* sort, so the remap is the identity;

Increase it in addPaletteColor and the 'Palette aus Materialien' button, and include it in serialize.ts export/import, so a deleted colour's code is never given to another colour.

findings.title: Custom palette: compute deletes unused colours and renumbers the user's colour codes for good
findings.problem: Requirement 7 asks for stable, unique colour numbers ('01=Weiss…') and own colours. In 'Eigene Palette' mode, computeMosaic drops every colour no stone uses, sorts the rest by lightness and assigns codes 1..n. useProject then stores this reduced palette as rec.palette and as the new computedWith. Unused colours (e.g. a yellow the user owns) are deleted with no message. Every printed code changes (Schwarz 02→07, Haut 04→02), so plans printed before a recompute no longer match the tile boxes the user labelled. Switching to 'Automatisch' and computing also overwrites the custom palette, because it is not stored separately.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t5_custom_palette_compaction.cjs, output t5_output.txt. BEFORE (8): '01=Weiss, 02=Schwarz, 03=Mein Gruen, 04=Haut, 05=Braun, 06=Mein Blau, 07=Rot, 08=Gelb'. AFTER (7): '01=Weiss, 02=Haut, 03=Mein Gruen, 04=Mein Blau, 05=Rot, 06=Braun, 07=Schwarz' (Gelb deleted), 'stale badge: false'. Code: mosaic.ts:560-577 (filter by used, sort by L*, code = ni+1, applied in every mode), useProject.ts:331-339 (palette replaced, computedWith recomputed from the reduced palette).
findings.proposal: In custom and materials modes, return the input palette unchanged: keep every entry, its order and its user code, and report usage via stats (0 stones). Apply the keep/sort/renumber only for 'auto' and 'auto-snap'. Store the user palette separately (rec.customPalette) so the mode switch and auto computes do not destroy it. Copy codes from the input FixedColor (add a `code` field) instead of ni+1. Add a vitest case: a custom palette of 8 colours with one unused gives 8 entries with the same codes after compute.
corrected:
1. src/core/mosaic.ts: add an optional `code?: number` to FixedColor. In the final palette block, when `params.paletteMode === 'custom'`:
   - skip the filter, sort and remap;
   - return every input entry in input order, with `code: fixed[i].code ?? i + 1`, the same lab/hex/name/materialId, and data indices unchanged (they already point into the input palette).
   Leave the current keep/sort/renumber for 'auto' and 'auto-snap'. For 'materials' mode, keep removing unused entries so the legend does not fill with the whole library. If you want stable codes there too, keep material-list order instead of L* order.
2. src/ui/project/useProject.ts:295: pass `code: p.code` into fixed. After compute in custom mode, keep r.palette's codes. Line 339 then just uses computeKey(next) unchanged.
3. Optional (M): add `customPalette?: PaletteColor[]` to ProjectRecord (src/core/types.ts, serialize.ts round-trip).
   - Write it whenever setPalette runs in custom mode.
   - In custom mode, compute from customPalette.
   - When switching back to 'custom', restore rec.palette from customPalette, so an 'auto' compute no longer destroys the user's own colours.
4. UI and PDF: unused custom colours stay in the palette table with 0 stones (StepColors already shows stats.perColor[i]). The PDF material list already filters `pieces > 0` (pdf.ts:373). Optionally mark 0-count rows as "nicht verwendet" in the legend instead of hiding them.

   - Adding a 9th colour and recomputing leaves codes 1..8 unchanged.
   - computeStats totals still equal the stone count.

(a) src/core/mosaic.ts: add an optional `code?: number` to FixedColor. In the block at lines 550-577, only for `params.paletteMode === 'custom'`: keep every index (no `used` filter), skip the L* sort, and set `code: fixed[old].code ?? ni + 1`. findings.title: 'Palette aus Materialien' after a compute swaps the palette without remapping stones, so the whole mosaic changes colours (black face)
findings.problem: In custom-palette mode, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button calls api.setPalette() with a freshly built array in material order. The computed mosaic stores palette indices, and compute had already re-sorted the palette by lightness. Every stone therefore silently gets another colour: the face becomes black and the hair light blue. The preview, the stats and the PDF all use the scrambled mapping. Only the generic stale badge appears. Other paths that change palette length or order without remapping can produce indices ≥ palette.length.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t12_palette_replace_after_compute.cjs, output t12_output.txt. Before: '02 Haut hell 300 | 03 Hellblau 1.176 | ... | 10 Schwarz 215'. After: '02 Schwarz 300 | 03 Haut hell 1.176 | ... | 10 Grau 215 | 11 Gruen 0 | 12 Rosa 0'. Same stone counts, different colours. Side-by-side t12-before-after.png in the same folder. Code: StepColors.tsx:144-155 (setPalette(p) with no remap, even when api.computed exists); compare removePaletteColor in edits.ts:174-193, which does remap.
findings.proposal: Add a remapPalette(oldPalette, newPalette, data, formula) helper to edits.ts. It maps each old index to its new index by materialId, then exact hex, then nearest ΔE, and rewrites c1/c2/sub/free via remapAll. Call it from every palette-replacing action when api.computed is set ('Palette aus Materialien', and any future import), followed by touchMosaic(). Otherwise disable the button after compute, with the hint 'Erst neu berechnen'. Add an invariant check (max index < palette.length) in the loader and before PDF/CSV generation, and show an error instead of printing wrong colours.
corrected:
The direction is right. Here it is made precise:

(4) Add a vitest that computes in custom mode, replaces the palette in another order with fewer entries, applies the remap, and then checks two things: every index is below palette.length, and the stats piece total still equals the total from geometry.

1) StepColors.tsx:144-152, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button. When api.computed is null, keep today's replace behaviour. When api.computed exists, MERGE so that existing indices and codes stay stable:

   If you want a single helper, put mergePaletteFromMaterials(palette, data, materials, formula) in edits.ts. It returns {palette, movedStones, maxDeltaE} and is built from addPaletteColor and removePaletteColor. Do not build a full reorder remap, since that renumbers codes and makes printed sheets wrong.
2) Invariant guard. Add assertPaletteIndices(data, palette) to src/core/edits.ts (or types.ts). It scans c1/c2 (only where kind uses them), sub and free, and returns the maximum index. Call it:

   On a violation, do not print magenta stones or undercounted totals. Show a clear error ('Farbzuordnung beschädigt – bitte neu berechnen'), block PDF/CSV export and offer a recompute.
3) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
   - Compute in custom mode from 12 materials, run the merge, and assert that every piece keeps its hex, total pieces are unchanged and all indices are < palette.length.
   - Run the merge with a shrunk material list and assert that the moved-stone count equals the stones of the removed colours and that the total is unchanged.
   - buildCsv and buildPdf throw on out-of-range indices.
   Reproduction of the current failure modes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-correctness-ui-state-3/remap_check.ts.

findings.title: No undo/redo and no area or batch editing: every correction is one irreversible single-stone click
findings.problem: Requirement 13 (manually change stones, e.g. 'lighter blue') can only be done one piece at a time, and nothing can be undone. Removing a palette colour remaps every stone permanently. A shape change clears that cell's laying progress. A core function to replace a colour within a range already exists but is not reachable from the UI. Correcting a sky or a background means hundreds of separate clicks with no safety net.
findings.evidence: Reproduction /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/b1.cjs. Output: 'color before: 03 | after change: 04 | after ctrl+z: 04'. Grep finds no undo in src except 'free.undoPoint' (the freeform point editor). replaceColor in src/core/edits.ts:209 has no caller in src/ui. removePaletteColor is called from src/ui/project/StepColors.tsx:112. setCellKind sets progress to 0 (src/core/edits.ts:77). The README table lists 'Rückgängig (Undo): nicht vorhanden'.
findings.proposal: Add an EditJournal in src/core/edits.ts. Each operation stores CellSnapshot{idx, kind, c1, c2, sub?, line?, free?, progress} before and after; only the few affected Map entries are cloned. Palette operations store the previous palette plus the (idx, piece, oldColor) tuples they changed. Cap the stack at about 200 operations or 32 MB. Add ↶/↷ buttons in Preview and Plan, Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, and 'letzten Tap zurück' in laying mode. Add a selection tool in Viewer: a rectangle or lasso in mm, selecting by piece-centroid test. Actions on the selection or section: 'Farbe A → B' (reuse replaceColor with Range); 'heller/dunkler', which picks the palette colour with the smallest ΔE among those with L* ≥ current+3 or ≤ current−3; and 'Form zurücksetzen'. Each batch is one journal entry. Stats are recomputed by the existing worker path.
corrected:
Deliver this in three phases. Phase A is cheapest and helps most.

**Phase A (S): batch colour replacement and two data-loss fixes.**
- **Section panel** (StepPlan.tsx, next to the existing mark/reset buttons, around lines 205-225): add "Farbe A → B in diesem Abschnitt". Section already has r0/r1/c0/c1, so pass it straight to replaceColor(c.layout, c.data, from, to, sec), then call api.touchMosaic() and show the returned count.
- **Palette table** (StepColors.tsx): add "alle Steine dieser Farbe → Farbe X" for the whole mosaic, without deleting the colour (replaceColor with no range).
- **Confirm before deleting a colour** (StepColors.tsx remove()): show a confirm() that names the stone count and the target colour code.
- **Stop needless progress resets** (edits.ts setCellKind): return early without touching anything when the kind is unchanged (for LINE, also with the same parameters; for SUB, also with the same k). Also keep progress for a FULL ↔ DIAG change only if a future decision allows it. The minimum fix is: do not clear progress on a no-op.

**Phase B (M): undo and redo.**
- **Journal module.** Add src/core/editJournal.ts, kept in memory and cleared whenever computeMosaic produces new data.
- **Cell operations.** For setPieceColor, setCellKind, setFreePieces, togglePiecePlaced, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced and replaceColor, store per-cell before/after snapshots: {idx, kind, c1, c2, progress, sub?, line?, free?}, with the Map entries cloned. A batch operation becomes one entry holding many snapshots.
- **Palette operations.** For removePaletteColor (and updatePaletteColor), store the previous palette array. For removal, also store only the pieces that had the removed colour, as (idx, piece). Undo works in two steps: first map every colour value v ≥ removedIndex back to v + 1 across c1, c2, sub and free (the inverse of remapAll), then restore the recorded pieces to removedIndex. As a simpler alternative, snapshot packMosaic(data) for palette operations only; that is about 8 MB at 2 M cells.
- **Limits.** Cap the journal at about 200 entries or about 32 MB and drop the oldest first.
- **UI.** Add ↶/↷ buttons in StepPreview and StepPlan. Bind Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z only when focus is not in an input field. After every undo or redo, call touchMosaic or touchProgress so stats are recomputed through the existing worker effect (useProject.ts:239ff) and the change is saved.

**Phase C (M): rectangle selection in Viewer.**
- **Selection mode.** A toggle that turns drag-to-pan into drag-to-select. Convert the mm rectangle into a row/col Range using layout.colX and layout.rowY, so stats.Range is reused.
- **Actions.** "Farbe A → B" (replaceColor with that range), "Form zurücksetzen" (setCellKind FULL for each cell), and "heller/dunkler". For each piece, "heller/dunkler" picks the existing palette colour with the smallest ΔE2000 among those with L* ≥ L*cur + 3 (or ≤ L*cur − 3). Pieces with no such colour stay unchanged and are counted in the result message. No new colours are ever invented.
- **Undo.** Each action is one journal entry.
- **Lasso.** Defer it. If it is added later, select pieces by a centroid-in-polygon test.

**Tests.** In tests/, check that undo after each operation restores packMosaic output byte for byte, and that progress totals are unchanged after undo.

Phase 0 (S, ship first): guard the destructive actions.
- StepColors.tsx:108 remove(): count how many stones use the colour (api.stats.perColor[i].pieces) and find the target through the same NearestColorMatcher as removePaletteColor. Then call confirm(t('colors.removeConfirm', {n, code, name, targetCode, targetName})), e.g. "203 Steine von 09 Hellblau werden zu 10 Blau. Fortfahren?". Also let the user choose the replacement colour; removePaletteColor already takes a `replacement` argument.
- StepPlan.tsx:210 "Abschnitt fertig": ask confirm() when the section already has partial progress.

Phase 1 (M): EditJournal, a new file src/core/journal.ts, pure TS with vitest tests.
- Entry types:
  - CellsEntry: struct-of-arrays, not objects. idx: Uint32Array; kind/c1/c2/progress before and after as typed arrays; side maps of sub/line/free clones only for the affected idx. Used for setPieceColor, setCellKind, setFreePieces, replaceColor in a range, and batch shape reset.
  - PaletteRemoveEntry: {prevPalette, removedIndex, target, slots}. `slots` holds only the raw slots that held removedIndex: c1 indices, c2 indices, (subIdx, q) and (freeIdx, k). Undo = shift every index ≥ removedIndex up by 1, then write removedIndex back into those slots, then restore prevPalette. This round-trips exactly (verified in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-spec-gaps-3/journal-proto.ts) and its memory grows with the number of stones of that one colour, not the whole project.
  - PaletteEntry {prev, next} for updatePaletteColor, matchAll and add.
- Rules:
  - The stack is LIFO and redo is cleared on every new entry.
  - compute() in useProject.ts clears both stacks. Optional extra: keep the previous packMosaic plus palette as one "Neuberechnung rückgängig" entry, stored in IndexedDB under 'mosaic-prev' so it is not held in RAM.
  - Cap by bytes (~32 MB) and by entries (~200), dropping the oldest.
  - The journal lives in memory only and is cleared when the project is closed; say so in the README.
- useProject exposes undo()/redo()/canUndo/canRedo. Applying an entry calls touchMosaic() (and setPalette for palette entries), so the existing worker stats path recomputes totals. No count or geometry is derived from the journal itself.
- UI:
  - ↶/↷ buttons in StepPreview, StepPlan and StoneDialog.
  - Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y, ignored while focus is in an input.
  - StoneDialog re-reads its cell after undo.
- Progress gets its own separate small stack in StepPlan laying mode, with a button "Letzten Tap zurück" (togglePiecePlaced is its own inverse; setRangePlaced stores the previous progress slice as a Uint16Array per section row range).
- Update README.md:152 to describe the new state.

Phase 2 (M): batch editing.
- Viewer gets a "Auswählen" toggle. Only in that mode does a one-finger/mouse drag draw a rectangle instead of panning. The rectangle snaps to whole cells via indexAt and yields a Range {r0, r1, c0, c1}.
- Scope choices: selection, current section (existing sec range), or whole project.
- Actions, each one CellsEntry:
  1. "Farbe A → B" through replaceColor(layout, data, from, to, range). Before applying, show the number of affected stones as a dry run.
  2. "Heller/Dunkler": per source colour in the selection, pick the palette colour with the smallest ΔE among palette colours with L* ≥ L+3 (or ≤ L−3). Only existing palette colours are used. If none qualifies, show "Keine hellere Farbe in der Palette – bitte Farbe hinzufügen" instead of inventing one. Before applying, show the mapping, e.g. "09 → 05 (ΔE 4,1)".
  3. "Form zurücksetzen (ganzer Stein)" through setCellKind FULL. Warn when the selection contains laid stones, because their progress will be cleared (undo restores it).
- Lasso selection and per-piece selection are deferred to a later step.
- Tests:
  - undo/redo round-trip equality of packMosaic after mixed sequences (colour, kind, free, palette remove, range replace).
  - stats.pieces unchanged by colour batches, and per-colour counts sum to the total.
  - memory of a palette-remove entry ≤ 8 bytes × stones of that colour.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
